directoryStems.mcq-d332a08b6fe7baa4d221260c: בן 78, מתהלך, סובל מדמנציה בינונית, מתגורר במחלקה לתשושי נפש. חזר למחלקה לאחר אשפוז בבית חולים כללי, שם היה שבוע מרותק למיטה ונזקק לחיתול. כעת ללא שליטה על שתן. מהו הטיפול הנכון בשבילו?
directoryStems.mcq-7c2dad0adf8d1917ff506524: בן 85, עם רקע של הגדלת ערמונית שפירה (BPH), מגיע למרפאה עם אי-נקיטת שתן כרונית. מתלונן על כך ש"תמיד רטוב" ולא שם לב מתי נותן שתן. בעת ההשתנה בשירותים, מתאר קושי במתן שתן, בעיקר בהתחלה וסובל מטפטוף. מהי האבחנה הסבירה?
directoryStems.mcq-16901cf73d684c18a48a5302: בת 70, ברקע אי ספיקת לב וסוכרת, התקבלה במרפאתך בגלל אירועים תכופים של בריחת שתן. לדבריה, אלה מתרחשים ללא אזהרה, בדרך כלל בהקשר של שיעול או עיטוש. איזו מההתערבויות הללו היא בעלת הסבירות הגבוהה ביותר לסייע בבריחת שתן?
directoryStems.mcq-77e6ef73149271bca24a7601:
בת 89, מאושפזת לשיקום לאחר שבר ב RAMUS PUBIS. ברקע מחלת לב איסכמית, יתר לחץ דם והיפרליפידמיה. באשפוז הופעת גרד עורי והוחל טיפול באנטיהיסטמין. כעת מטופלת בתרופות הבאות:   
 TARGIN (OXYCODONE/NALOXONE) 10 mgX2  
 LERCANIDIPINE (VASODIP) 10 mgX2  
 MIRTAZAPINE (MIRO) 15 mgX2  
 OMEPRADEX 20 mgX2  
 BISOPROLOL (CARDILOC) 1.25 mgX1  
 LORATADINE (LORASTINE) 10 mgX1  
 OXAZEPAM (VABEN) 10 mgX1  
 CALCIUM 600 mgX1  
 VITAMIN D 2000 unitsX1  
 המטופלת מתקדמת בתהליך השיקומי ומתהלכת בהשגחה עם הליכון. מתלוננת על בריחת שתן ללא קשר לשיעול או צחוק. בנוסף, זרם השתן חלש מהרגיל, ובלילה מתעוררת כל שעתיים לשירותים. שוללת עצירות. בדיקת שארית על ידי BLADDER SCAN מדגימה שארית של 300 סמ"ק. מהו הצעד הראשון שיש לנקוט בו, כדי לשפר בצורה הטובה ביותר את ההפרעה בנקיטת שתן שמתוארת?
directoryStems.mcq-2bed597c32fe379c447c85c9: A 78-year-old woman leaks urine when coughing, sneezing, or laughing, without preceding urgency. She toilets independently and has a low postvoid residual. Which type of incontinence best fits?

directoryStems.mcq-0981df60817848c93ee89b8b: After removal of a urinary catheter, a woman cannot empty her bladder and has a residual volume of 600 mL. Which action matches Hazzard's bladder-retraining protocol?
directoryStems.mcq-dadaa773e1ea18be3bb9bdee: An 82-year-old woman with stress urinary incontinence has learned to contract her pelvic floor muscles correctly. How should she use this skill when she anticipates coughing?
directoryStems.mcq-0d2d6814b0802a6ee6df9449: A 72-year-old woman leaks urine with coughing and lifting but has no urgency or frequency. Which next step addresses the leakage mechanism after failure of nonsurgical treatment?
directoryStems.mcq-8abd221d4504584009908109: A 78-year-old man with prostatic enlargement has urinary leakage and a repeatedly measured postvoid residual of 350 mL. His blood pressure is uncontrolled. Which approach addresses the chronic retention described?
directoryStems.mcq-1b0192a332196e360df7c59d: A 68-year-old postmenopausal woman has irritative voiding symptoms, urgency, and urgency incontinence with atrophic vaginitis and urethritis. directoryStems.mcq-850127ed700137db3455a85e: A 75-year-old woman has mixed urinary incontinence with both stress and urgency symptoms. Frequent urgency-related leakage bothers her much more than occasional stress leakage. Her postvoid residual is normal. Which initial treatment priority is appropriate?
directoryStems.mcq-f9524b46b1a938ac2f210cf3: An 82-year-old man has continuous leakage and stress urinary incontinence that substantially affect his quality of life two years after radical prostatectomy. Pelvic floor exercises and conservative treatment for 18 months have not helped. Which intervention directly addresses urethral closure?
directoryStems.mcq-d6e5b9f87cb177c3b7771d54: A healthy, active 70-year-old woman has persistent urgency incontinence despite behavioral treatment and trials of several anticholinergic drugs over the past year. She wants a minimally invasive option before considering major surgery. Which procedure is described for refractory urgency incontinence?
directoryStems.mcq-426f4be5da0b79e0f434eeba: A 74-year-old man with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment has urgency incontinence. His family wishes to avoid an antimuscarinic drug. His postvoid residual is 180 mL and blood pressure is 128/78 mmHg. Which listed bladder relaxant acts through beta-3 receptors?
directoryStems.mcq-e2a9f5ace31e635c39772ebc: A 69-year-old woman with mixed incontinence uses a controlled, slow-release vaginal estrogen ring for atrophic vaginitis. After an initial short course she reports partial improvement in irritative symptoms. Which advice follows Hazzard's description of topical treatment?
directoryStems.mcq-8f584ee3ce842acb33aee5ca: A 71-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia has taken tamsulosin for six months. Urgency has improved, but postvoid residual remains 280 mL and he has occasional overflow incontinence. He asks about adding an anticholinergic for residual urgency. If surgical consultation is considered for persistent outflow-related symptoms, which approach does Hazzard describe?
directoryStems.mcq-09722781a8f941ee67fd502b: An 83-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities is considering sacral neuromodulation for urgency incontinence that has not improved with treatment. Which statement accurately describes this intervention?
directoryStems.mcq-ec3e36817a72912dba9ba902: A long-term indwelling catheter is necessary after other drainage options have been assessed. Which urinary complication becomes increasingly likely with prolonged use?
directoryStems.mcq-d2c4133cef12fdb043ab2fad: An 86-year-old man with Parkinson disease, BPH and recurrent falls takes carbidopa–levodopa, tamsulosin, oxybutynin and mirtazapine. He has dry mouth, severe constipation, hesitancy and a postvoid residual of 250 mL. Which medication change best addresses this combination?
directoryStems.mcq-7e4a2cd9400c0e8231db7ab7: A 76-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia is undergoing a trial without catheter. He has difficulty voiding and a postvoid residual of 650 mL. directoryStems.mcq-978e7beb65683db410749b4e: An 89-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate dementia and osteoporosis develops agitation and pulls at his clothing. Temperature is 37.1 degrees C, blood pressure 156/92, and heart rate 88. He has not passed urine for 12 hours, and bladder scan shows 850 mL. Which approach addresses a potentially reversible medication contribution while providing toileting assistance?

Which approach addresses the metabolic contributor described by Hazzard?

Which medication-review principle should guide the discussion?

Her daughter and healthcare proxy asks about a catheter to reduce distress. Which circumstance is a listed indication for considering a chronic indwelling catheter?
directoryStems.mcq-4ffaaaf7e18c4ea72232aa40: After removal of an indwelling catheter, an older patient has persistent frequency, nocturia, and urinary leakage. His medicines were recently changed. According to Hazzard's bladder-retraining protocol, what should precede a trial of a bladder relaxant?
directoryStems.mcq-e0bdc251ee2d28c1c47b0686: A 78-year-old woman with COPD requiring home oxygen and HFpEF has mixed urinary incontinence: leakage while hurrying to the toilet and during coughing. directoryStems.mcq-91774f31cea353009ae41738: A 79-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment takes oxybutynin for urgency incontinence. directoryStems.mcq-95d90103995305ae519c4834: An older woman starts mirabegron for overactive bladder. Which pair of adverse effects listed by Hazzard warrants attention to blood pressure and pulse?

directoryStems.mcq-379a9a2cc64ace39cdba952b: Intermittent catheterization is being considered for a woman with urinary retention. Which management principle follows Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-e67ed6d39b3de3192047448f: A 77-year-old man with Parkinson disease and benign prostatic enlargement develops constipation, confusion, and urinary retention after starting tolterodine. Which combination supports concern about a drug effect?
directoryStems.mcq-4f4625a874aa961cce3eafe8: An older man with Alzheimer disease develops confusion, dry mouth, and constipation after starting oxybutynin. Which explanation is consistent with the drug effects listed in Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-898befeca3d6842bac71fb5c: An 80-year-old man with prostate cancer develops urinary retention. PSA is 28 ng/mL and postvoid residual is 450 mL. Which medication change removes an anticholinergic bladder relaxant that can contribute to retention?

highlightAliases.new: Oxybutynin (antimuscarinic) 2.5–5 mg tid — dry mouth, blurry vision, ↑ intraocular pressure, delirium, constipation (p712); patients with dementia must be followed for drug-induced delirium (p713); Current practice (not the book): offer an antimuscarinic or beta-3 agonist for OAB (Strong recommendation, Grade A); counsel on side effects and potential dementia/cognitive risk with antimuscarinics (Clinical Principles), using shared decision-making and patient preferences; when pharmacotherapy is indicated, consider a beta-3 agonist trial first, as typically preferred in the guideline discussion - AUA/SUFU 2024, statements 16-18 and discussion, p24-27

highlightAliases.new: Vaginal estrogen ring — 1 ring every 3 months, for atrophic-vaginitis-related urgency UI; Table 47-12 (p712) lists a history of gynecologic cancer as a contraindication and breast cancer as a relative contraindication. In practice, cancer type and treatment matter. After inadequate relief with nonhormonal treatment, selected breast-cancer survivors may choose low-dose vaginal estrogen after a risk–benefit discussion. For patients taking an aromatase inhibitor, involve the oncologist in that decision. ACOG clinical consensus, 2021. See AGS Beers 2023 required-article card for systemic versus low-dose vaginal estrogen and the breast-cancer discussion qualification (Table 2, p2061)

highlightAliases.new: PVR interpretation: PVR < 100 mL without straining generally reflects adequate emptying; PVR > 200 mL abnormal; 100–200 mL is equivocal (p707).

highlightAliases.old: Mirabegron (beta-3 agonist) 25–50 mg qd (p712) — beta-3 agonists should not be used in uncontrolled hypertension (p714).
highlightAliases.new: Mirabegron 25–50 mg once daily for overactive bladder, with renal/hepatic dose adjustment when appropriate. Monitor BP. US labeling advises against mirabegron in severe uncontrolled hypertension (systolic ≥180 or diastolic ≥110 mm Hg). This warning is drug-specific (pp712,714; FDA mirabegron prescribing information).

highlightAliases.old: Constipation is technically < 3 bowel movements/week (p717); the most common causes of fecal incontinence are constipation and laxative use, neurologic disorders, and colorectal disorders (p716); relieving a fecal impaction can resolve urinary as well as fecal incontinence (p701).
highlightAliases.new: Fewer than 3 spontaneous bowel movements/week is one feature of constipation. Hard stool, straining or incomplete evacuation can occur even with daily bowel movements (p717). Common contributors to fecal incontinence include constipation/impaction, laxative use, and neurologic or colorectal disorders (p716). Relieving impaction can improve both urinary and fecal incontinence (p701).
